title: Declarative RBAC Graph Engine + Authorization Gatekeeper (runtime middleware & audit enrichment)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a declarative, graph-based RBAC engine that compiles customer policy manifests into an evaluable graph and ship a lightweight Authorization Gatekeeper middleware inside the runtime process (no sidecar) that enforces decisions, propagates SSO/SAML context, and emits enriched audit events to the centralized logging pipeline. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and a stagged rollout for host API, console, and Dedicated runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Engine accepts declarative policy manifests (YAML/JSON) and compiles to a deterministic evaluation graph
Gatekeeper middleware responds to authorization queries within latency budget: P95 add < 3ms for cached decisions on 10k RPS node
Audit events produced include actor/source, resolved principal from SAML assertions, policy id/version, decision path, and redaction markers
Admin console can view recent authorization events for a resource and drill into policy decision traces
Feature rolled out behind a runtime feature flag and canary gate; fall back to existing authorizer paths without downtime
implementation_plan: Design: finalize graph schema (nodes: subject, resource, action, condition, temporal) and a compact bytecode for fast evaluation - design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Sec/RBAC+Graph+Engine
Compiler: implement manifest->graph compiler in Go (runtime service), include validation and deterministic hashing for policy versioning
Cache layer: in-memory TTL cache with prefix/KV-aware keys and watch-based invalidation from policy store
Gatekeeper: embed a low-overhead middleware in the runtime request path that performs decision lookup, instrumentation, and emits structured audit events
SSO/SAML propagation: add connectors to map SAML attributes into graph attributes; enrich audit events with assertion id and tenant binding
Audit pipeline: enrich events with policy trace and redact PII via configured redaction rules before sending to ELK/Kafka
Admin UX hooks: add endpoints for decision trace retrieval and event sampling to console API
testing_plan: Unit tests for compiler and graph evaluator (edge cases: cycles, contradictory rules, temporal windows)
Integration tests: runtime middleware with policy store and cache invalidation
Load tests: synthetic 10k RPS decision-per-request profile to measure P50/P95/P99 latency and CPU impact
Security fuzzing: random attribute inputs, malformed SAML assertions, replay attempts
E2E: canary rollout validating audit event content and console trace visibility
roll_out_plan: Phase 0: deploy compiler and policy store changes to staging; admin UI behind feature flag
Phase 1: enable Gatekeeper on 5% canary nodes for non-critical tenant traffic; enable verbose audit sampling
Phase 2: ramp to 25% after perf/observability validation; enable SAML attribute mapping for test tenants
Phase 3: full roll to hosted API and console; optional opt-in for Dedicated customers; monitor budgeted cost metrics
Rollback: flip runtime feature flag and invalidate cache; legacy authorizer remains available for 30 minutes of fallback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased request latency if graph evals are not optimized; Mitigation: compiler emits optimized execution order and we add per-node memoization
Risk: audit events leak PII; Mitigation: apply redaction rules in the pipeline and scope sampling so full traces are restricted to Security role
Risk: policy migration gaps for legacy rules; Mitigation: compatibility shim that translates old ACLs and a migration validator
Risk: SAML attribute mismatch causing denial of service; Mitigation: safe-fail mode where missing attributes fall back to attribute-defaults and log for admin review
